title: Low-energy collective electronic excitations in a gold monolayer
abstract: The low-energy plasmonic properties of a free-standing Au(111) monolayer, frequently referred to as goldene, are investigated by time-dependent density functional theory in the random phase approximation. In the evaluation of dielectric and loss functions the first-principle band structure characterized by a single $s-p$ energy band at the Fermi level is taken into account. In this system with apparently simple band structure around the Fermi surface the calculations show the presence, besides the standard two-dimensional (2D) plasmon mode, at even lower energies of three anomalous branches in the momentum-energy region usually assigned to incoherent electron-hole pairs. This is an unexpected result since the electronic system of the gold monolayer is characterized by a single energy band crossing the Fermi level. The dispersion of these anomalous plasmonic branches is strongly anisotropic in-plane and gapless. A general feature is that at small in-plane momentum transfers the modes have a sound-like dispersion in certain momentum directions. We rely the appearance of these anomalous modes to a notable deviation of the Fermi surface of a gold monolayer from a circular shape. As a result of its almost perfect hexagon shape, there is possibility to realize in a {\it single} electronic energy band a scenario of a multi-component electron system with the carrier groups moving with different Fermi velocities in certain momentum directions. The found modes correspond to the out-of-phase charge oscillations of the carriers at different sides of the hexagonal Fermi surface. Hence our work presents evidence how in a metal system with apparently simple band structure around the Fermi level its shape can result in conversion of single-particle charge excitations into collective charge excitations.

summaries.en: Time-dependent density functional theory reveals that a free-standing gold monolayer (goldene) with a single band crossing the Fermi level hosts, besides the standard 2D plasmon, three anomalous gapless and strongly anisotropic collective plasmonic branches at low energies, arising because its nearly hexagonal Fermi surface converts single-particle excitations into out-of-phase collective charge oscillations.

title: 'Dancing' two-dimensional patterns in nematics above the flexoelectric instability threshold
abstract: Various types of electrohydrodynamic instabilities in liquid crystals (LCs) are a recurring theme in LC research. The nonlinear stage of the flexoelectric instability in nematics remains the least studied aspect of this phenomenon. This work highlights a key advancement in nonlinear physics, providing a compelling example of nonlinear dynamical system behavior. By solving the system of nonlinear equations for a nematic in an alternating external field, we derive from first principles the unique "dancing" behavior of truly two-dimensional patterns above the flexoelectric instability threshold. Our analysis is restricted to liquid crystals with negative dielectric permittivity and electrical conductivity anisotropies. The resulting solution represents a stable limit cycle near above the Hopf bifurcation, valid within the parameters range where the solutions characteristic exponent is complex. The generalized two-dimensional Ginzburg-Landau-like phenomenological theory of the phenomenon is developed.

summaries.en: Solving the nonlinear equations for a nematic with negative dielectric and conductivity anisotropies in an alternating field yields a stable limit cycle just above the Hopf bifurcation that explains the 'dancing' behavior of truly two-dimensional patterns above the flexoelectric instability threshold, supported by a generalized two-dimensional Ginzburg-Landau-like phenomenological theory.

title: Sub-monolayer tracking of molecular states at buried interfaces
abstract: Phenomena responsible for emerging technologies originate from novel molecular states at buried interfaces. Yet quantitatively resolving these features is out of reach in most cases. Resonant scattering has demonstrated sensitivity to these local states but is limited due to a lack of accurate interpretive models. We leverage a machine learning (ML)-optimized optical model to analyze polarized resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) from molecular thin films. This new analysis establishes the direct and quantitative interpretation of molecular orientation, chemical identity and packing states as a function of depth with sub-monolayer resolution - reaching beyond the diffraction limit via locking energy and polarization through the optical model. From our analysis, we discover a gradient evolution of molecular orientation and packing emerging from the interface, indicative of competing surface versus bulk growth dynamics and contradicting hypotheses of substrate patterning. This nondestructive insight into buried interfacial formation and final state opens possibilities in controlling interfacial states and phenomena in next-generation technologies.

summaries.en: A machine-learning-optimized optical model enables quantitative sub-monolayer-resolved analysis of polarized resonant soft X-ray scattering, revealing gradient evolution of molecular orientation and packing at buried interfaces that contradicts substrate-patterning hypotheses.

title: Structural characterization of the rutile-GeO2/TiO2 (001) heterointerface
abstract: Rutile-GeO2 (r-GeO2) has emerged as a promising ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) semiconductor for future high-power device applications because of its favorable combination of physical and electrical properties. This study has used high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) to compare heterointerfaces between thin films of GeO2 grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition on closely-lattice-matched rutile TiO2 (r-TiO2) substrates at temperatures of 840° C and 925° C. Cross-sectional TEM observations reveal interfaces with two entirely different structures: an amorphous GeOx/r-TiO2 heterostructure with an abrupt, highly faceted and non-planar interface, or a fully epitaxial r-GeO2/r-TiO2 heterostructure characterized by a more wavy but often facetted interface. Structural analysis of the latter sample revealed a high density of strain-relieving interfacial dislocations, identified primarily as Lomer-type or 60°-type, that accommodated the ~4% lattice mismatch between the two materials, while chemical analysis showed very limited interfacial intermixing. Crystallographic analysis showed that the interface faceting was associated with rutile {101} facets, with characteristic facet angles of ~114°; these observations support thermally driven TiO2 (001) substrate faceting rather than an interface reconstruction resulting from GeO2 epitaxy. Overall, these findings provide useful insights into the mechanisms governing interface formation and strain relaxation in r-GeO2/r-TiO2 heterostructures and suggest that further refinement of growth conditions should enable improved epitaxial growth of r-GeO2 for future ultrawide-bandgap electronic device applications.

summaries.en: High-resolution TEM reveals that GeO2 films grown on rutile TiO2 (001) form either an amorphous GeOx/r-TiO2 interface with abrupt, highly faceted, non-planar boundaries or a fully epitaxial r-GeO2/r-TiO2 interface with wavy {101}-faceted boundaries and a high density of Lomer- or 60°-type dislocations that relieve the ~4% lattice mismatch with limited intermixing.

title: Spatiotemporally-resolved differential dynamic microscopy reveals strain-induced deformations in heterogeneous soft materials
abstract: Understanding the microscopic behavior of materials in response to mechanical perturbations is a central challenge in soft matter, yet existing methods, which typically rely on microscopy-based imaging, often struggle with spatial heterogeneity and low signal-to-noise that are characteristic of many soft and biological materials. Additionally, many existing rheo-optical methods focus on the response to macro-scale forces rather than localized perturbations despite the importance of local stresses in biological and industrial applications of soft materials. Here, we present STroboscopically Averaged, time-Resolved Differential Dynamic Microscopy (starDDM) to investigate a sample's deformation across time and distance due to a cyclically applied local force. As proof-of-principle, we use this model-independent and tracer-free approach to map the motions of active cytoskeleton composites imposed by the movement of an optically trapped probe particle embedded within the complex network. We reveal how motor-driven restructuring and varying strain rates tune the magnitude and propagation of the response, which we further show decays with distance from the perturbation. This analytical platform fills a critical gap in micro-rheology, offering a versatile tool for probing the non-equilibrium dynamics of soft materials ranging from biopolymer networks to 3D-printed materials and soft robotics.

summaries.en: The paper introduces starDDM, a model-independent and tracer-free differential dynamic microscopy method that maps spatiotemporally resolved deformations induced by a locally applied cyclic force, demonstrated by probing optically trapped probe-driven strain responses in heterogeneous active cytoskeleton composites.

title: Heterogeneous superconductivity emerging from a charge-stripe state in kagome lattices
abstract: Charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity have long been recognized as competing orders. However, recent achievements establish that the interplay between these two collective electronic phenomena can be more perplexing, with emergent phenomena arising from their cooperation. Here we report a distinctive case of the kagome superconductors CsV3Sb5-xSnx, in which the characteristics of superconductivity evolve in accordance with the form of CDW order. As the triple-Q CDW in CsV3Sb5 transforms to a short-range stripelike CDW at xc = 0.07, a sudden change in superconducting properties occurs concomitantly. A combination of thermodynamic, electrical transport and scanning tunneling microscopy experiments reveals a heterogeneous superconducting state beyond xc: the superconducting gap exhibits pronounced spatial variation, in conformity with a distribution of critical temperature and the resulted superconducting precursor effects. Moreover, abundant normal fluid persists deep into the superconducting state, as evidenced by remnants of electronic specific heat and zero-energy quasiparticle interference. These observations are unrelated to the chemical inhomogeneity and residual strain effect introduced by Sn substitution. Instead, they emulate the phenomenology that a sign-changing superconducting order parameter is subject to strong pair-breaking scattering with the short-range charge stripes and hence reflect the unconventional nature of superconductivity developing inside the charge-stripe state.

title: Interface Control of Second-Harmonic Generation in Layered CuInP2S6 via PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3 Domain Wall
abstract: The control of nonlinear optical responses in van der Waals ferroelectrics at the nanoscale offers opportunities for developing two-dimensional integrated nanophotonics with programmable functionalities. In this work, we report the first realization of nanoscale nonvolatile control of the amplitude and polarization of second-harmonic generation (SHG) response in layered CuInP2S6 (CIPS) via the domain structure in an interfacial PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3 (PZT) thin film. The SHG intensity at CIPS/PZT heterointerface is continuously modulated, either substantially enhanced or almost entirely quenched, by the circular domain walls in underlying ferroelectric oxide. The interfacial coupling of CIPS polar axis with in-plane polarization of PZT domain walls tailors the SHG light polarization into two-fold (C2V) symmetry, which is well modeled by nonlinear electromagnetic theory. Overall, this study enables nonvolatile programmable design of nonlinear light intensity and polarization in van der Waals ferroelectrics at the nanoscale.

title: Intrinsic Raman Modes and Crystal Symmetry of Altermagnetic $α$-MnTe
abstract: Crystal symmetry governs the physical properties of materials and provides the framework for interpreting their microscopic excitations and macroscopic responses. In altermagnets, the crystal symmetries that relate opposite-spin sublattices give rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting despite compensated magnetization. Determining the real crystal symmetry is therefore essential for understanding the intrinsic electronic and magnetic properties. For the altermagnetic semiconductor ${\alpha}$-MnTe, conflicting Raman assignments have left both its intrinsic lattice excitations and its crystal symmetry unresolved. Here we combine high-resolution Raman and second-harmonic generation (SHG) spectroscopy with first-principles calculations to distinguish intrinsic lattice excitations from Te-derived spectral contributions and to examine bulk inversion symmetry of ${\alpha}$-MnTe. We show that several prominent Raman features previously assigned to ${\alpha}$-MnTe instead originate from segregated Te clusters or precipitates. The remaining intrinsic Raman response consists of a single Raman-active mode assigned to the calculated $E_{2g}$ phonon, consistent with the centrosymmetric $D_{6h}$ symmetry. The SHG response agrees with surface electric-dipole and bulk electric-quadrupole contributions expected for a centrosymmetric $D_{6h}$ crystal, supporting the preservation of bulk inversion symmetry in ${\alpha}$-MnTe. Our findings revise the Raman assignments in ${\alpha}$-MnTe and provide a basis for interpreting its altermagnetic properties within the appropriate crystal-symmetry framework.

summaries.en: High-resolution Raman and SHG spectroscopy combined with first-principles calculations shows that prominent Raman features previously assigned to altermagnetic α-MnTe arise from segregated Te clusters, leaving a single intrinsic E2g Raman mode consistent with centrosymmetric D6h symmetry and bulk inversion symmetry.

title: Flexo-Photoresponses from First Principles
abstract: Many functionally important materials, such as silicon, possess high-symmetry crystal structures that forbid even-order nonlinear optical responses, thereby limiting their application in e.g., photonics and optoelectronics. Strain gradients can effectively break symmetries, activating otherwise forbidden optical responses. Although such flexo-photoresponses have attracted considerable interest recently, a comprehensive microscopic theoretical framework is still lacking. Here, we develop a first-principles approach that can systematically evaluate a wide range of flexo-photoresponses in realistic materials. By mapping strain gradients to long-wavelength phonons within the established theory of electron-phonon coupling, our approach captures the nonlocal quantum-mechanical effects of lattice deformations on nonlinear optical responses. Applying the framework to prototypical centrosymmetric materials, including Si, cubic $\rm SrTiO_3$, and monolayer black phosphorus, we demonstrate that a strain gradients of $10^5\sim10^6~\rm m^{-1}$ can induce flexo-second-harmonic generation and flexo-bulk photovoltaic effects comparable to the intrinsic responses of non-centrosymmetric crystals. Our work establishes a rigorous foundation for strain gradient engineering of light-matter interactions, opening new avenues for nanoscale optomechanics, optoelectronics, and beyond.

summaries.en: The authors develop a first-principles framework that maps strain gradients to long-wavelength phonons via electron-phonon coupling to capture nonlocal quantum effects and systematically evaluate flexo-photoresponses, showing that strain gradients of 10^5-10^6 m^-1 induce flexo-second-harmonic generation and flexo-bulk photovoltaic effects in centrosymmetric materials such as Si, cubic SrTiO3, and monolayer black phosphorus comparable to intrinsic responses of non-centrosymmetric crystals.

title: Electron Wavefronts Capture Nanoscale Movies of Hypersound at Surfaces
abstract: Acoustic waves transport mechanical energy and elastic strain through solids, with material composition and shape governing their propagation. In the gigahertz hypersound regime, acoustic wavelengths reach tens to hundreds of nanometres, comparable to nanoscale device dimensions. Harnessing these waves underpins high-frequency signal processing, sensing, electromagnetic coupling and quantum control. Acoustic metrology probes elastic modes and internal interfaces. Yet directly imaging how nanoscale acoustic waves interact with local structure remains challenging, requiring picometre displacement sensitivity combined with high spatiotemporal resolution. Here we demonstrate full-field imaging of laser-induced hypersound at surfaces using reflected electron wavefronts. We introduce ultrafast low-energy electron microscopy (ULEEM), exploiting the intrinsic surface sensitivity of few-electronvolt electrons. Coherent electron pulses down to femtosecond durations reflect from the topmost atomic layers, imprinting the evolving surface profile onto their wavefronts. Defocus converts phase variations into image contrast. In a thin van der Waals material, we image the thermoelastic generation and propagation of picometre-amplitude acoustic waves. Measured dispersion relations, interpreted through elastodynamic modelling, distinguish substrate-supported and locally detached regions, revealing how interfacial contact shapes propagation. Delayed wave emission reveals scattering at buried mechanical defects. Our results establish electron-wavefront imaging of nanoscale surface dynamics, enabling the exploration of ultrafast energy transport, structural transformations and coupled mechanical, electronic and magnetic phenomena.

title: Side-Chain Engineering Controls Molecular Packing and Vertical Electron Transport in Discrete n-Type NDI-T2 Oligomers
abstract: High-efficiency vertical charge transport in multilayer organic optoelectronic devices highly depends on molecular structure and arrangement. Using two T2-(NDI-T2)2 conjugated oligomers with ethylhexyl (EH) and octyldodecyl (OD) side chains as a model system, their effects on electron transport are investigated using, among other techniques, atomic force microscopy (AFM), conductive atomic force microscopy (C-AFM), grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS), steady-state optical spectroscopy, and time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations. The oligomers of both materials exhibit relatively disordered structures in the as-cast state, whereas annealing enhances structural order and leads to side-chain-dependent changes in molecular stacking. EH-based films show a smaller annealing-induced photoluminescence shift than OD-based films, suggesting less pronounced stacking and conformational rearrangements, consistent with TDDFT-supported exciton analysis. The current-voltage characteristics are analyzed using the space-charge-limited current (SCLC) model. After annealing, both materials exhibit improved vertical electron mobility. The EH-based films reach a maximum mobility of 1.2 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1. The combined results suggest that the shorter EH side chains modify the out-of-plane packing environment and facilitate vertical electron transport. These results establish a structure-property relationship between side-chain structure, molecular order, exciton coupling and vertical mobility, providing a molecular design basis for optimising organic semiconductors through side-chain engineering.

title: Modification of optical properties in ultrathin ALD-grown NbN layers using oxygen plasma treatment
abstract: NbN thin films with a nominal thickness of 10 nm were grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) on Al$_2$O$_3$-buffered Si substrates and treated with oxygen plasma for 0 s (untreated), 20 s, 40 s, and 60 s to investigate oxygen-induced changes in their optical properties. Spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) measurements were performed before and after oxygen plasma treatment over the ultraviolet-visible-near-infrared (1.24-6.20 eV) and infrared (0.041-0.827 eV) spectral ranges. Film thickness determined by X-ray reflectivity (XRR) was used as a fixed parameter in the optical modeling to extract the dielectric function, optical constants, and effective free-carrier concentration. We observed the emergence of a distinct absorption feature near 4.9 eV following oxygen plasma treatment, consistent with the oxidation of the NbN surface and the resulting change in its optical properties. Increasing the treatment time from 0 to 60 s reduced the effective carrier concentration from $1.20 \times 10^{22}$ to $1.03 \times 10^{22}$ cm$^{-3}$ and the effective carrier mobility from 2.44 to 2.27 cm$^2$ V$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$. The obtained results provide a basis for understanding the effects of oxygen plasma treatment on NbN thin films.

title: High-quality, deep formation and identification of oxygen-vacancy defects in silicon carbide
abstract: Optically addressable paramagnetic defects in silicon carbide (SiC) are attractive for scalable quantum technologies such as quantum sensing. PL5, PL6, and PL7 are promising defects for their high brightness and spin-readout contrast. Although generation by oxygen implantation has been reported very recently, nonuniform spin and optical properties and the limited generation depth of implanted defects hinder both high-sensitivity sensing and conclusive microscopic identification. Here we engineer high-quality defects by decoupling oxygen incorporation and defect formation, realizing highly homogeneous spin-resonance frequencies as well as narrow optical linewidths and long T2* coherence time. Further, we demonstrate defect formation beyond the ion range utilizing oxygen diffusion, exceptional among impurities in SiC. We further provide hyperfine-interaction statistics of 17O and host nuclei across many PL6 defects, making the oxygen-vacancy origin conclusive. Together, the microscopic identification and the demonstrated formation route establish a foundation for developing the oxygen-vacancy spin defect into a versatile quantum platform.

summaries.en: By decoupling oxygen incorporation from defect formation, the authors achieve highly homogeneous spin-resonance frequencies, narrow optical linewidths, and long T2* coherence times in optically addressable oxygen-vacancy defects in silicon carbide, demonstrate defect formation beyond the ion range via oxygen diffusion, and confirm the oxygen-vacancy origin through hyperfine-interaction statistics of 17O and host nuclei.

title: Rationalizing charge transfer: a single-molecule case study across three distinct surfaces
abstract: Organic molecules are versatile building blocks for the formation of complex low-dimensional nanostructures on surfaces. Recently, interest has grown in translating on-surface synthetic protocols from noble metal surfaces to insulating surfaces, which offer technological relevance, and to magnetic or superconducting surfaces, which offer new routes to correlated phases. It is important, therefore, to understand how these alternative surfaces may alter the properties of adsorbates through processes like charge transfer and screening. Evidence for charge transfer is often obtained experimentally via scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS), and theoretically via density functional theory (DFT). In this work, we systematically compare the properties of isolated macrocyclic emeraldine (Me$_6$) molecules on three different surfaces: metallic Au(111), a semiconducting ferromagnetic monolayer of FeCl$_2$, and a cleaved superconducting surface of bulk 2H-NbSe$_2$. We show that STS and DFT alone are insufficient to quantify charge transfer for these cases. Instead, we complement these methods with Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) measurements and model Hamiltonian calculations to demonstrate that on Au(111) and FeCl$_2$, Me$_6$ molecules donate a single electron to the substrate, whereas on NbSe$_2$ two electrons are transferred from molecule to substrate. Our work provides insight into the interplay of charge transfer, screening, and molecule-substrate coupling, and develops experimental and theoretical methods for comparing the properties of adsorbates across different surfaces for future studies.

summaries.en: By combining scanning tunneling spectroscopy, density functional theory, Kelvin probe force microscopy, and model Hamiltonian calculations, this single-molecule study shows that macrocyclic emeraldine (Me6) molecules donate one electron to Au(111) and to a ferromagnetic FeCl2 monolayer but two electrons to superconducting 2H-NbSe2.

title: Multiport photonic routing with a single cavity-based electro-optic phase shifter per port
abstract: Programmable photonic meshes can perform general linear transformations, but universal transformations on $N$ modes require $O(N^2)$ programmable phase shifters, which cannot simultaneously achieve low drive voltage, gigahertz speed, zero static power, lossless modulation, and a compact footprint. Signal routing does not require universal transformations, which allows considerable circuit simplifications. We present a compact reflective circuit architecture that connects all input-output pairs across $N$ modes in $N$ steps using only $O(N)$ programmable phase shifters. The circuit comprises a single passive $N\times N$ interferometer and a single column of programmable reflective phase shifters. We demonstrate the architecture by implementing a $3\times 3$ router in x-cut thin-film lithium niobate with a passive multimode interferometer and phase shifters based on single-sided photonic-crystal nanobeam cavities. Our programmable devices exhibit a $1.92$ GHz/V resonance tuning efficiency via the Pockels effect, a footprint of $100\,\mu\mathrm{m}^2$, sub-5-V drive voltage, and a 6.2 GHz electro-optic bandwidth. Through voltage-space characterization and physical modeling, we identify routing states with extinction ratios exceeding 11 dB at each output and demonstrate sequential routing at an equipment-limited speed of 10 MHz. Our results establish cavity-enhanced Pockels switching as a routing layer for classical and quantum computing interconnects across visible and near-infrared wavelengths.

title: Thermal-noise-limited stabilization of a self-injection-locked diode laser using a miniature Fabry-Perot cavity
abstract: We present an ultrastable laser system based on miniature core components: a self-injection-locked laser comprising a distributed-feedback laser diode and an integrated microring resonator, together with a 3-ml vacuum-gap Fabry-Perot cavity. By carefully addressing technical noise sources, in particular residual amplitude modulation, we demonstrate a thermal-noise-limited fractional frequency instability of $5\cdot10^{-15}$ for averaging times between 1 and 10 s, which is among the lowest reported for compact cavity-stabilized lasers. This performance is achieved with conventional multilayer mirrors and a moderate cavity finesse of $10^5$. Such stability of the output frequency, combined with the small size of the core components and a possibility to generate a Kerr frequency comb in the very same microring resonator, provides a path towards fully integrated photonic frequency references for transportable optical clocks and low-noise microwave synthesis.

summaries.en: Using a self-injection-locked distributed-feedback diode laser with an integrated microring resonator and a 3-ml vacuum-gap Fabry-Perot cavity, the authors achieve a thermal-noise-limited fractional frequency instability of 5×10⁻¹⁵ for averaging times of 1 to 10 s, among the lowest reported for compact cavity-stabilized lasers.

title: RADICAL: Reconfiguration-Aware Direct-Connect AI Cluster using Spatial-and-Wavelength Selective Switching
abstract: We present RADICAL, the silicon-photonic-enabled Reconfiguration-Aware Direct-Connect AI Cluster that integrates a custom spatial-and-wavelength selective switch (SWSS) with the Linux network stack. RADICAL deploys a packaged 4x4x4$\lambda$ microring-based SWSS into a four-GPU-server cluster using standard SFP28 optical transceivers, and a reconfiguration-aware host-networking interface to demonstrate a direct-connect reconfigurable optical fabric. The SWSS provides dynamic spatial and wavelength routing with 3.2-6.8 dB path loss, average wavelength and spatial crosstalk isolation exceeding 25 dB, and error-free 25 Gbps signal recovery across routing paths. At the system level, RADICAL validates reconfiguration-aware operation through continuous bulk data transfers totaling 6.4 TBytes over 10 minutes. We further demonstrate multitenant AI training across reconfigurable link topologies, including four ResNet-18 instances and six nanoGPT instances, with the latter sustained for more than five hours.

title: Cross-coupled photon avalanche drives room-temperature intrinsic optical bistability
abstract: Optically bistable materials promise technological advances in optical information processing, memristive devices, and multiparametric sensing. However, optical bistability is predominantly observed under cryogenic conditions or is governed by subtle thermo-optical nonlinearities. Here, we report on Ho3+-activated nanocrystals that exhibit cavity-free intrinsic optical bistability (IOB) at ambient conditions. Non-thermal IOB stems from a cross-coupled photon avalanche (XPA) mechanism enabled by a low-phonon-energy double-perovskite host, which reduces nonradiative losses and facilitates excited-state population via XPA, even when the pump intensity is below threshold. Time-resolved luminescence measurements support the proposed XPA, as evidenced by a double-rise profile consistent with two reservoir states interlocked in energy looping. IOB with high-contrast photoswitching (up to 46 dB) is observed at room temperature across multiple visible emission lines, enabling wavelength-division multiplexing and compatibility with common detectors. IOB is preserved across nano- to microscale crystals and different double-perovskite compositions, broadly enabling information photonics and advanced sensing.

summaries.en: Ho3+-activated double-perovskite nanocrystals exhibit cavity-free intrinsic optical bistability at room temperature via a cross-coupled photon avalanche mechanism, enabling high-contrast photoswitching up to 46 dB across multiple visible emission lines.

title: Single-step SU(3) Hahn Echo in a Qutrit Atom Interferometer
abstract: The Hahn echo is a well-known dynamical decoupling method that refocuses the dephasing due to energy inhomogeneities of a spin-1/2 ensemble and is widely used to extend phase coherence in quantum computers and sensors. Extensions of such techniques beyond the spin-1/2 have been reported, but have mainly used SU(2) gates, limiting their scalability. Here, we generalize the Hahn echo to qutrits using single-step SU(3) gates and extend the coherence time by more than an order of magnitude. The gates are generated through optimal control theory and implemented in an ultracold atomic ensemble in free fall. A quantum process tomography procedure benchmarks the gates and yields fidelities of ~ 93%, limited mainly by state preparation and measurement errors. Due to the geometry of the laser beams, the generalized Hahn echo also realizes a three-path Mach-Zehnder atomic interferometer with two independent interferometric phase differences. Our results therefore establish SU(3) control for dynamical decoupling of qutrits and multi-path atom interferometers, with the latter opening the possibility for vector force measurements and interferometric tests of the validity of Born's rule.

summaries.en: The authors generalize the Hahn echo to qutrits using single-step SU(3) gates generated by optimal control theory and implemented in a free-falling ultracold atomic ensemble, extending coherence time by over an order of magnitude with gate fidelities of about 93% and realizing a three-path Mach-Zehnder atom interferometer with two independent phase differences.

title: Revealing and Mitigating Transmittance and Reflectance Errors in Integrating-Sphere Characterization of High-Albedo Scattering Media
abstract: Accurate optical characterization of high-albedo scattering media is fundamentally limited by integrating-sphere measurement errors. Scattering events spatially redistribute photons, leading to lateral beam spread and angular divergence that bias measured reflectance and transmittance. Here, we investigate these deviations, which are quantified and interpreted by using the point spread function (PSF), guided by the radiative transfer equation. Experiments and Monte Carlo modelling show that the widely used external-mount integrating-sphere configuration introduces systematic, configuration-dependent errors that become pronounced when scattering-induced lateral spreading is substantial. Using a normalised PSF to quantify photon redistribution, we map the characteristic lateral spreading length across a broad $(\taus,g)$ parameter space in the high-albedo limit, providing a basis for evaluating errors in specific measurement geometries. We further quantify the influence of measurement geometry and show that, in the pencil-beam limit, maintaining $L/D_{\mathrm{port}}\lesssim 0.01$ reduces the discrepancy arising from the finite collection aperture to approximately \qty{1}{\percent}. In addition, we introduce an internal-mount integrating-sphere protocol that suppresses scattering-related losses and yields transmittance and reflectance measurements in good agreement with theoretical predictions. Overall, our work helps users of integrating-sphere measurements identify scattering-related errors and improve the reliability of transmittance and reflectance characterization across a wide range of application areas.

summaries.en: This study uses a point spread function guided by the radiative transfer equation, supported by experiments and Monte Carlo modelling, to quantify and map the scattering-induced lateral spreading that causes systematic, configuration-dependent errors in external-mount integrating-sphere reflectance and transmittance measurements of high-albedo media, and it introduces an internal-mount protocol that suppresses these losses and agrees well with theoretical predictions.

title: Perfectly aperiodic asymmetric scalable metasurface based on the hat monotile
abstract: Metasurfaces are conventionally designed on periodic lattices, which renders their electromagnetic response spatially uniform and leaves the spatial arrangement itself unused as an information-bearing design resource. In this study, we propose and numerically validate a metasurface built on an aperiodic monotile: the recently discovered "hat" polykite, a single tile mathematically guaranteed to tile the plane only nonperiodically. The twelve distinguishable orientations of the hat serve as a natural design basis; each carries resonant elements tuned to one of twelve absorption frequencies between 4.600 and 4.914 GHz, transcribing the provable aperiodicity and mirror asymmetry of the geometry into the electromagnetic response. Gaussian-beam scanning over a compositionally unique 6 times 6 grid yields irregular, position-dependent electromagnetic signatures whose pairwise separations reach beyond 6 dB. In particular, coherence-guided selection of multiple frequencies increases the stable rank of the position-signature matrix from 1.0 to approximately 1.6 with three frequency components, whereas the accumulation of mutually similar electromagnetic features fails to add effective dimensions, demonstrating that properly selected multifrequency characteristics enhance the spatial distinguishability embedded in the surface. A shift-correlation analysis in which the cosine similarity never exceeds 0.5 confirms that the response inherits the absence of translational order from the tiling. Compatible with standard printed-circuit fabrication, the aperiodic metasurface design establishes a deterministic route toward position-identifiable electromagnetic environments for localization, chipless identification, and integrated sensing and communication.

title: From Hollow Waveguides to Mie Voids: Low-Index Light Confinement
abstract: The confinement of light within optically thin media challenges the conventional view that optical localization requires high-index dielectric materials and total internal reflection. Over the past decades, a broad range of photonic phenomena has demonstrated that electromagnetic energy can also be guided and localized inside low-index regions or nanoscale void cavities. What first appears to be a curiosity is, in fact, highly relevant: The interaction between light and matter lies at the heart of much in optics and photonics. It enables sensing, nonlinear optical phenomena, and optical manipulation, yet it also inevitably introduces absorption, dissipation, and loss. Pushing localized, enhanced, or guided energy into a lower-index space thus offers entirely new possibilities for light-matter interaction and dispersion control. In this review, we discuss some of these counterintuitive structures, starting with light guidance within optically thin media, such as hollow-core photonic crystal fibers or antiresonant reflecting optical waveguides. We then discuss the optics of bubbles, that is, low-index inclusions in a higher-index surrounding, and ultimately arrive at the so-called Mie void resonators, optical resonators that support localized electromagnetic modes confined within a region of lower refractive index. All these systems demonstrate that there are (resonant) optics beyond simple total internal reflection. Absence can itself become a functional photonic degree of freedom, opening opportunities across sensing, quantum nanophotonics, metasurfaces, and programmable optical matter.

summaries.en: This review describes counterintuitive photonic structures—hollow-core waveguides, low-index inclusions, and Mie void resonators—that confine and guide light within lower-index regions, showing that resonant optics can transcend total internal reflection and that absence itself can serve as a functional photonic degree of freedom for sensing, quantum nanophotonics, metasurfaces, and programmable optical matter.

title: Stochastic Analysis of Laser Phase Noise in Photonics-Assisted Radio Frequency Beamforming
abstract: This paper develops a stochastic model for quantifying the impact of laser phase noise on photonics-assisted radio frequency (RF) beamforming. Unlike conventional deterministic models, the presented theoretical framework captures the statistical randomness associated with the RF array factor of beamforming networks driven by finite-linewidth lasers. Fourier-domain analysis reveals that laser phase noise reshapes the spatial coherence function of such beamforming networks, inducing coherent RF aperture shrinkage, beam-pattern distortion, and directivity degradation. The analysis highlights that beamforming network architectures employing nanosecond-scale optical differential delays can exhibit substantial performance degradation even when driven by commercially available narrow-linewidth (kHz-range) lasers. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that average RF power gain gets downscaled and fluctuations dominate in large-aperture beamforming networks due to phase noise, imposing an upper limit on the maximum achievable RF antenna array-size. The reported results highlight the quantitative performance and scalability limits imposed by laser phase noise in photonics-assisted RF beamforming, offering key design guidelines for implementing large-scale beamforming networks in next-generation wireless communications, sensing, radar, and radio astronomy applications.

summaries.en: This paper presents a stochastic model showing that laser phase noise reshapes the spatial coherence function of photonics-assisted RF beamforming networks, causing coherent aperture shrinkage, beam-pattern distortion, and directivity degradation even with kHz-linewidth lasers and nanosecond optical delays, thereby imposing an upper limit on the achievable RF antenna array size.

title: Computational imaging through turbid, bubbly and flowing water near the telescope
abstract: Cameras in the surf zone or behind ship wakes look through turbid, bubbly, moving water close to the lens, yet restoration networks are usually scored only on displayed images. We introduce a measured dataset of a telescope viewing displayed images and physical objects through a 25~mm water layer 45~mm in front of its objective, under seven combinations of flow, bubbles and turbidity, with clear-water recordings as a second reference. Because the suspension scatters light far outside the 1.3\textdegree{} field of view, turbidity mainly removes contrast, 4.4- to 4.8-fold on a Siemens star. Restoring the mean of eight frames improves structural similarity (SSIM) by 0.032 over a single frame, and learned fusion of the frames adds little. One raw frame supports five-category recognition (96.8\%) as well as restored images. Adding synthetic training pairs leaves display-image scores unchanged but raises the correlation of a restored Siemens star with its clear-water recording from below 0.5 to above 0.9. These networks also improve ordinary underwater photographs without retraining, where training on measured pairs alone fails. Scoring against the digital source or a clear-water recording reverses the ranking of raw and restored images. These results support a simple pipeline: average the frames, classify raw frames directly, and restore with networks trained on measured and synthetic pairs.

title: Supercontinuum-driven broadband Fourier-transform photothermal microspectroscopy
abstract: Chemical characterization of microscopic samples often requires resolving multiple, widely separated vibrational absorption bands, including their positions and spectral shapes. Photothermal microspectroscopy provides a route to localized vibrational measurements by detecting absorption-induced thermal responses with a separate optical probe. However, rapid acquisition of broadband photothermal spectra remains challenging when spectral information is collected through sequential wavelength tuning. Here, we develop a supercontinuum (SC)-driven Fourier-transform photothermal (FT-PT) microspectroscopy platform that combines broadband near-infrared excitation with rapid-scan interferometric acquisition for localized vibrational measurements. In this approach, an interferometrically modulated SC pump induces wavelength-dependent photothermal responses in the sample, which are detected through a co-propagating visible probe beam and reconstructed by Fourier transformation. Using a 1.65-2.35 um spectral window, we demonstrate broadband photothermal spectra of aqueous samples with acquisition rates of approximately one spectrum per second. The system simultaneously resolves multiple molecular absorption features in a water-dimethyl sulfoxide mixture and reproduces the near-infrared absorption characteristics of liquid water with high spectral fidelity. Extending beyond homogeneous liquids, a dark-field detection configuration enables broadband photothermal spectroscopy of an individual 6 um polystyrene particle in an aqueous environment. This SC-based FT-PT microspectroscopy approach provides a rapid and broadband platform for localized vibrational characterization of liquid and microscopic samples, enabling chemical analysis with microscale spatial selectivity.

summaries.en: A supercontinuum-driven Fourier-transform photothermal microspectroscopy platform enables rapid broadband vibrational spectra of aqueous and microscopic samples at about one spectrum per second.

title: Integrated elliptical III-V nanopillar arrays on silicon for dual photodetection and light emission
abstract: Next-generation on-chip photonic devices require compact, energy-efficient components integrating photodetection and light emission on silicon platforms. Achieving broadband photodetection combined with efficient emission in a single nanoscale device remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate elliptical nanopillar arrays monolithically integrated as III-V-on-Si templates, exhibiting broadband photoresponse across visible to near-infrared wavelengths, dynamic neuron-like graded responses under modulated light, and pronounced electroluminescence at around 865 nm under forward bias. The nanostructured elliptical geometry approach enhances optical absorption and carrier dynamics within an active area significantly smaller than commercial detectors, enabling responsivities up to 0.55 A/W at 830 nm in compact nanoarrays. This work advances the development of miniaturized active nanophotonic devices suitable for integrated sensing, emitting and communication circuits, and neuromorphic processing on silicon substrates.

title: Video-rate quantitative phase and polarimetric imaging (QP2I) for label-free imaging of contracting muscle cells
abstract: Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) has become a standard approach for label-free microscopy of transparent specimens, mapping the optical path length. However, the isotropic phase is blind to the molecular order underlying optical anisotropy. Implementations that also add quantitative contrast to birefringence, rely on multi-frame illumination or polarization-state scanning, or on dedicated interferometric hardware, that trade away acquisition speed or the simplicity of a standard microscope. We present Quantitative Phase and Polarimetric Imaging (QP2I), a computational imaging framework that converts a standard differential interference contrast (DIC) microscope with a polarization camera into a single-shot, video-rate, dual-contrast imaging system. We developed a new globally regularized phase reconstruction that eliminates artifacts of prior DIC-to-QPI approaches, providing quantitative phase information and used per-pixel Stokes-based reconstruction to obtain quantitative anisotropic retardance. We validate the approach across simulations, static reference targets, fixed muscle tissue and living dynamically moving cells. Thereby, QP2I enables to study contractile dynamics in live cardiomyocytes all-optically and label-free. It provides both structural and functional readouts at frame rates that are sufficient to temporally resolve fast cardiomyocyte contractions. While conventional fluorescent labels bleach out over time, perturb physiology, and preclude long-term monitoring, QP2I provides similar established structural readouts, such as frame-by-frame sarcomere length, as well as previously inaccessible measurements, like quantitative analysis of retardance changes during muscle contraction, as a direct optical signature of muscle photoelasticity. QP2I thus enables long-term, label-free interrogation of dynamic cellular processes at quantitative contrast.

summaries.en: QP2I is a computational imaging framework that turns a standard differential interference contrast microscope with a polarization camera into a single-shot, video-rate system for label-free quantitative phase and anisotropic retardance imaging, enabling all-optical study of contractile dynamics in live cardiomyocytes.
summaries.zh: QP2I是一种计算成像框架，可将配备偏振相机的标准微分干涉相差显微镜转变为单次拍摄、视频速率的系统，实现无标记的定量相位与各向异性延迟成像，从而能够全光学地研究活体心肌细胞的收缩动力学。

title: A Compact Single-Beam Optically Pumped Magnetometer Based on Absorption Detection
abstract: We demonstrate a compact single-beam optically pumped magnetometer (OPM) employing a pure 87Rb microfabricated vapor cell with 500 Torr buffer gas. The residual magnetic field is actively minimized to below 400 pT through a combination of mu-metal magnetic shielding and internal compensation coils. We systematically characterize the OPM response as a function of laser detuning and optical intensity, and derive the magnetic-field sensitivity from the signal slope and noise amplitude spectral density. A best sensitivity of 11 fT/Hz^1/2 is achieved near the resonance transition at an optimal optical intensity, using a small cell volume of only 0.027 cm^3. Furthermore, a miniaturized OPM prototype was developed using a folded flexible printed circuit board (FPCB) to integrate the vapor cell, a compact heater, and magnetic-field coils into a cubic sensing head. Two coil configurations patterned directly on the FPCB were investigated. Under optimized operating conditions, the OPM prototype achieved a sensitivity of 66 fT/Hz^1/2. These results demonstrate that high-buffer-pressure single-beam OPMs can achieve excellent sensitivity, establishing a pathway toward compact and scalable arrays.

summaries.en: A compact single-beam optically pumped magnetometer using a pure 87Rb microfabricated vapor cell with 500 Torr buffer gas achieved 11 fT/Hz^1/2 sensitivity near resonance at optimal optical intensity, and a miniaturized folded-FPCB prototype integrating the cell, heater, and coils reached 66 fT/Hz^1/2.
summaries.zh: 基于纯87Rb微加工蒸气池和500 Torr缓冲气体的紧凑型单光束光泵磁力计在共振跃迁附近的最佳光强下实现了11 fT/Hz^1/2的灵敏度，而采用折叠柔性印刷电路板集成蒸气池、加热器和磁场线圈的小型化原型达到了66 fT/Hz^1/2的灵敏度。

title: Scaling the Wavelength to Optimize Ultrafast Laser Processing of Bandgap Materials
abstract: The spectral characteristics of ultrashort laser pulses offer unique possibilities to control interactions in space and time as well as the subsequent material responses. In particular, selecting the wavelength predefines the fundamental mechanisms governing laser-matter interaction, and thus, how energy is deposited. This Chapter provides an overview on how the essential physical effects in ultrafast laser-matter interaction scale with the wavelength, and the consequences for bandgap material processing applications. First, we recall the main spectral properties of bandgap materials and discuss the important question of the expected processing resolutions depending on wavelength. Then, recent studies on the impact of the wavelength in ultrafast laser-dielectric interaction are presented. Finally, we present how the latest developments in infrared ultrafast laser sources can be advantageously utilized to internally process narrow-gap materials despite challenges related to increased nonlinearities.

summaries.en: This chapter reviews how the fundamental physical effects in ultrafast laser-matter interaction scale with wavelength and discusses the consequences for processing bandgap materials, including processing resolution, recent studies on wavelength impact in dielectric interaction, and the use of infrared ultrafast sources to internally process narrow-gap materials despite increased nonlinearities.
summaries.zh: 本章综述了超快激光与物质相互作用中的基本物理效应如何随波长缩放，并讨论了其对带隙材料加工的影响，包括加工分辨率、波长在电介质相互作用中影响的最新研究，以及利用红外超快光源在内部加工窄带隙材料时所面临的非线性增强挑战。
summaries.ja: 本章では、超短パルスレーザーと物質の相互作用における基本的な物理効果が波長にどのように依存するかを概観し、加工分解能、誘電体相互作用における波長の影響に関する最近の研究、および非線形性の増大という課題を伴いつつ赤外超短パルス光源を用いて狭ギャップ材料を内部加工する方法など、バンドギャップ材料加工への影響を論じる。

title: Graphical Rigidity of Continuous Variable Graph States under Gaussian Local Transformations
abstract: Multimode entangled pure Gaussian states are an essential resource for continuous variable (CV) quantum information processing. Menicucci et al. [2011] have shown how to describe them as graphs with complex adjacency matrices. Among such complex graph states (CGSs), quantum optics experimental setups straightforwardly display correlations described by purely imaginary graph states (iRGSs) whereas theoretical literature favors off-diagonal real graph state (RGS) descriptions, which actually reflect the entanglement structure in the infinite squeezing limit [Gonzalez-Arciniegas et al. 2021]. We study them beyond this ideal case, thus establishing in the finite squeezing regime an equivalence criterion for the generic case of CGSs through a graph propagating set of conditions which either finds a Gaussian Local Unitary (GLU) converting one state to another or gives a proof of impossibility if such a GLU does not exist. In the experimentally relevant case of the conversion between iRGSs and RGSs, the set of conditions results in simple relations between the topologies of the equivalent real and imaginary graphs. Finally, we show that the canonical forms of iRGSs and RGSs imply that the topology of the CV real and imaginary graph states are too rigid to admit any exact qumode local-addition analogue to the qubit complementation or qudit local-addition, thus demonstrating the non-existence of any exact qumode local-addition for these states. We however define an approximate one when the squeezing is strong enough.

summaries.en: This paper establishes a graph-propagation equivalence criterion for finite-squeezing continuous-variable complex Gaussian graph states under Gaussian local unitary transformations, derives simple topology relations between purely imaginary and off-diagonal real graph states, and shows that the rigidity of their canonical forms precludes any exact qumode local-addition analogue to qubit complementation, though an approximate version exists for sufficiently strong squeezing.
summaries.zh: 本文为有限压缩情形下的连续变量复高斯图态建立了在高斯局域幺正变换下的图传播等价判据，推导出纯虚图态与实非对角图态之间简单的拓扑关系，并证明其规范形式的刚性使得不存在任何类似于量子比特取补的精确模式局域加法，但在压缩足够强时可定义一种近似操作。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、有限圧縮領域の連続変数複素ガウスグラフ状態に対し、ガウス局所ユニタリ変換の下でのグラフ伝播型等価判定基準を確立し、純虚グラフ状態と実非対角グラフ状態の間の単純なトポロジー関係を導くとともに、その標準形の剛性により量子ビットの相補化に相当する厳密なモード局所加法が存在しないことを示し、十分に強い圧縮では近似的なものを定義できることを明らかにする。

title: Robustness of Quantum Correlations and Controlled Teleportation Fidelity under Noisy Channels
abstract: In distributed quantum computing, quantum networks provide a potential infrastructure for long-range quantum information processing. Controlled quantum teleportation (CQT) is a key practically relevant protocol that can connect two parties on a network and enables a third party, the controller to allow or abort the secure teleportation of an arbitrary single-qubit state between the two parties. We investigate the robustness of a three-qubit GHZ resource under bit-flip, phase-flip, depolarizing, and amplitude-damping noise. Using the Kraus-operator formalism, we characterize the noisy resource through multipartite quantum discord, genuine multipartite concurrence (GMC), localizable entanglement (LE), and CQT fidelity. We also outline a proof-of-concept photonic implementation for preparing the three-qubit GHZ resource and realizing the CQT protocol, which could enable experimental investigation of the effects of noise. Our results show that bit-flip and amplitude-damping noise generally preserve useful mutipartite quantum correlations over broader noise parameter ranges. Interestingly, multipartite discord exhibits freezing under bit-flip noise over a finite parameter regime. Moreover, discord can persist beyond the sudden death of genuine multipartite entanglement, revealing the distinct robustness of nonclassical correlations. We further demonstrate that CQT fidelity which characterizes the performance of CQT can exceed the classical threshold even after GMC vanishes, while LE more closely reflects the operational usefulness of the noisy resource. These findings highlight the complementary roles of quantum correlations and entanglement in assessing the resilience of GHZ-based protocols.

summaries.en: Using Kraus-operator analysis of a three-qubit GHZ resource under bit-flip, phase-flip, depolarizing, and amplitude-damping noise, the study shows that bit-flip and amplitude-damping noise preserve multipartite discord and genuine multipartite concurrence over broader parameter ranges, discord can freeze under bit-flip noise and persist beyond entanglement sudden death, and controlled-teleportation fidelity can exceed the classical threshold even after genuine multipartite concurrence vanishes, while localizable entanglement better reflects operational usefulness.
summaries.zh: 该研究利用Kraus算符形式分析三量子比特GHZ资源在比特翻转、相位翻转、退极化与振幅阻尼噪声下的鲁棒性，发现比特翻转与振幅阻尼噪声能在更宽的参数范围内保持多体量子失谐和真正多体并发度，失谐在比特翻转噪声下可冻结并能在纠缠突然死亡后继续存在，且受控隐形传态保真度即使在真正多体并发度消失后仍可超过经典阈值，而可局域化纠缠更能反映资源的操作有效性。
summaries.ja: 本研究は、ビット反転・位相反転・脱分極・振幅減衰雑音下の3量子ビットGHZリソースをKraus演算子形式で解析し、ビット反転と振幅減衰雑音がより広いパラメータ範囲で多体量子ディスコードと真の多体コンカレンスを保持すること、ビット反転雑音下でディスコードが凍結し真の多体もつれの突然死後も持続しうること、さらに制御テレポーテーション忠実度が真の多体コンカレンス消失後も古典的閾値を超えうる一方で局所化可能エンタングルメントが動作上の有用性をよりよく反映することを示した。

title: Photon-Number Discrimination from Increasing Time-of-Arrival Separation in Wide Superconducting Microstrip Single-Photon Detectors
abstract: Measurements of photon-number-dependent time-of-arrival (TOA) distributions in wide NbN superconducting microstrip single-photon detectors (SMSPDs) are presented. Two \SI{10}{\um}-long devices with widths of \SI{3.2}{\um} and \SI{6.4}{\um} are characterized under pulsed \SI{515}{nm} excitation. The TOA histograms are described by sums of exponentially modified Gaussian (EMG) components, with the wider device exhibiting components assigned to photon numbers up to \(n=8\). Adjacent TOA peaks become more distinguishable relative to their widths at higher photon number, in contrast to the compression of neighboring photon-number timing shifts observed in conventional narrow-wire SNSPDs. For the components assigned to \(n=7\) and \(n=8\), the FWHM-normalized peak separation is \(2.15\), and the fitted EMG distributions yield an equal-prior pairwise TOA-assignment fidelity of \(99.6\%\). The EMG exponential-tail parameter \(\tau_n\) decreases strongly with photon number, while the Gaussian-location parameter \(\mu_n\) continues to shift between neighboring components. A phenomenological model motivated by absorption-site-dependent vortex processes and collective current redistribution captures these timing trends. These results support wide SMSPDs as a platform for TOA-based photon-number discrimination at high photon number, relevant to multiphoton-state characterization and photonic quantum information processing. The same geometry also provides a setting to examine how the spatial distribution of photon absorption affects vortex-assisted detection.

title: Bogoliubov Dynamics and Zitterbewegung in Optical Dirac Systems
abstract: We develop a bosonic Bogoliubov description of Zitterbewegung in time-dependent optical-Dirac systems. Within the optical-Dirac framework, the anomalous pair-creation and pair-annihilation terms of a bosonic Bogoliubov Hamiltonian correspond to couplings between the positive- and negative-frequency sectors, whose coherence underlies the Zitterbewegung response. When the constitutive parameters vary in time, the resulting moving-frame connection generates dynamical interbranch coupling and positive--negative-frequency coherence. Under periodic modulation, this coupling becomes resonant near $\Omega\simeq2\omega_0$, leading to parametric amplification of the coherence and consequently to an enhanced Zitterbewegung motion.

summaries.en: The paper develops a bosonic Bogoliubov description of Zitterbewegung in time-dependent optical-Dirac systems, showing that time-varying constitutive parameters generate interbranch coupling and positive-negative-frequency coherence that, under periodic modulation near Ω≃2ω0, is resonantly amplified, enhancing the Zitterbewegung motion.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了含时光学狄拉克系统中Zitterbewegung的玻色Bogoliubov描述，表明随时间变化的本构参数会产生分支间耦合以及正负频率相干性，并在Ω≃2ω0附近的周期调制下发生共振放大，从而增强Zitterbewegung运动。
summaries.ja: 本論文は時間依存の光学ディラック系におけるZitterbewegungのボソン的Bogoliubov記述を発展させ、構成パラメータの時間変化が分枝間結合と正負周波数間のコヒーレンスを生み出し、Ω≃2ω0付近の周期的変調下でこれが共鳴的に増幅されてZitterbewegung運動が増強されることを示した。

title: High Resolution Hyperspectral Quantum Infrared Imaging with Undetected Photons
abstract: Quantum sensing in the infrared regime often demands the use of expensive and cryogenically operated detectors. Nonlinear interferometry has paved the way for information transfer from the infrared to the near--infrared or visible regime in various quantum technologies. A particularly interesting application of these interferometers involves spectrally--resolved quantum imaging using undetected photons, enabled by the use of temperature--tunable parametric amplifiers. In this work, we demonstrate spectrally resolved transmission imaging with undetected photons around 1550 nm using a spontaneous parametric down conversion based folded nonlinear interferometric scheme, registering the attenuation of a zebrafish larva as a biological feasibility test. We characterize and calibrate the interferometer, having achieved spectrally resolved interference fringes with a maximum baseline visibility of $\sim 74\%$ in the near--infrared regime. Phase--stepped readout of a grating spectrometer gives a resolving power of $\sim1460$ (from the spectrometer's point spread function) at 1550 nm, and $\sim 730$ from the coherence length, the finest reported for imaging with undetected photons, over an instantaneous spectral window of $\approx 51$ cm$^{-1}$.

summaries.en: The paper demonstrates spectrally resolved hyperspectral transmission imaging with undetected photons near 1550 nm using a folded nonlinear interferometric scheme based on spontaneous parametric down-conversion, achieving near-infrared interference fringes with ~74% baseline visibility and a resolving power of up to ~1460 at 1550 nm over a ~51 cm⁻¹ instantaneous spectral window, validated by imaging the attenuation of a zebrafish larva.
summaries.zh: 该论文利用基于自发参量下转换的折叠非线性干涉方案，在1550 nm附近实现了未探测光子的光谱分辨高光谱透射成像，获得近红外干涉条纹最大基线可见度约74%，在1550 nm处分辨本领最高约1460，瞬时光谱窗口约51 cm⁻¹，并以斑马鱼幼体的衰减成像作为生物学可行性验证。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、自発パラメトリック下方変換に基づく折り返し型非線形干渉計を用いて、1550 nm付近の未被検出光子によるスペクトル分解ハイパースペクトル透過イメージングを実証し、近赤外で最大約74%のベースライン可視度の干渉縞を得るとともに、約51 cm⁻¹の瞬時スペクトル窓で1550 nmにおいて約1460の分解能を達成し、ゼブラフィッシュ幼生の減衰イメージングにより生物学的実現可能性を検証した。

title: Fundamental bound on Wigner negativity generation from environmental collisions
abstract: Beyond quadratic potentials, classical evolution laws are typically thought to arise from quantum theory as an approximate description. Here we show that classical evolution laws can emerge exactly, provided the environment interacts with the system via collisions. We use this to derive an inequality that lower bounds the distribution of environmental momentum kicks by the absolute value of the Fourier transform of the potential. We show that violating this inequality is necessary and sufficient for a non-quadratic potential to generate negativity from the set of positive Wigner functions. A simple consequence of this is a lower bound on the heating rate for a quantum system to evolve effectively classically. We illustrate our results using the theory of a levitated nanoparticle subject to photon recoil and background gas collisions. We derive the strength of external potential needed to generate Wigner negative states in an optical tweezer and propose an experimental test of whether a nanoparticle in an optical lattice is operating in a non-classical regime.

summaries.en: The paper shows that classical evolution laws can emerge exactly when the environment interacts with the system through collisions, and derives an inequality bounding the environmental momentum-kick distribution by the Fourier transform of the potential whose violation is necessary and sufficient for a non-quadratic potential to generate Wigner negativity from positive Wigner functions, implying a lower bound on the heating rate required for effectively classical evolution and proposing tests with levitated nanoparticles in optical tweezers and lattices.
summaries.zh: 该论文表明，当环境通过碰撞与系统相互作用时，经典演化规律可以精确涌现，并推导出一个用势的傅里叶变换绝对值下界约束环境动量踢分布的不等式，违反该不等式是非二次势从正Wigner函数集合产生Wigner负性的充要条件，由此得到量子系统有效经典演化所需加热速率的下界，并利用光镊和光晶格中悬浮纳米颗粒的实例提出实验检验方案。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、環境が衝突を通じて系と相互作用する場合に古典的発展則が厳密に現れ得ることを示し、環境の運動量キック分布をポテンシャルのフーリエ変換の絶対値で下から束縛する不等式を導出して、その違反が非二次ポテンシャルが正のウィグナー関数の集合からウィグナー負性を生成するための必要十分条件であること、ひいては有効的に古典的発展を実現するのに必要な加熱率の下限を与えることを示し、光ピンセットおよび光格子中の浮遊ナノ粒子を用いた実験的検証を提案する。

title: Quantum theory of laser noise in coherent-scattering levitated optomechanics
abstract: State purity is a key resource for experimental tests of quantum mechanics with massive objects. Cavity cooling of a levitated nanoparticle via coherent scattering stands out as a strategy to prepare highly pure states of its roto-translational motion. In several cases, though, the performance of cooling by coherent scattering is limited by the classical fluctuations of the laser field. Here we present a quantum theory of coherent-scattering experiments which includes the effect of the laser amplitude and phase noise. We derive a master equation for the noise-averaged particle's dynamics, valid for both center-of-mass and rotational degrees of freedom, and quantify the cooling performance for different levels of noise in state-of-the-art experiments. We compute approximate analytical expressions for the laser-noise-induced heating rates and excess phonon number in both regimes of weak and strong optomechanical coupling. Moreover, our model can be applied to laser noise processes with generic power spectral densities and finite correlation times. This work offers a toolbox to quantify and optimize the state purity in coherent-scattering experiments, and opens new avenues towards the preparation of quantum states with levitated systems.

summaries.en: This paper develops a quantum theory of coherent-scattering levitated optomechanics that incorporates laser amplitude and phase noise, deriving a master equation for the noise-averaged particle dynamics of both center-of-mass and rotational motion and providing analytical expressions for laser-noise-induced heating rates and excess phonon number in the weak and strong optomechanical coupling regimes.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了一种包含激光振幅噪声和相位噪声的相干散射悬浮光力学量子理论，推导了适用于质心与转动自由度的噪声平均粒子动力学主方程，并给出了弱、强光力耦合区由激光噪声引起的加热速率和多余声子数的解析表达式。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、レーザー振幅雑音と位相雑音を取り入れたコヒーレント散乱浮遊光力学の量子理論を提示し、重心および回転自由度に適用可能な雑音平均化された粒子ダイナミクスのマスター方程式を導出するとともに、弱結合・強結合光力学領域におけるレーザー雑音由来の加熱率と余剰フォノン数の解析的表現を与える。

title: Photon-Pair Advantage for Dissipative Parameter Estimation in Whispering-Gallery-Mode Interferometers
abstract: We study the estimation of detuning and intrinsic loss in a lossy whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) resonator located in a balanced Mach--Zehnder interferometer. We use indistinguishable photon pairs and coherent-state probes. We show that using indistinguishable photon pairs can provide higher Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) of dissipative parameters, such as intrinsic loss, at resonance away from critical coupling. Taking into account all photon-loss outcomes, we obtain analytical QFI expressions and compare photon-pair and coherent-state probe results when they have the same mean photon number. For estimating the round-trip amplitude transmission at resonance and away from critical coupling, the photon-pair probe gives a higher QFI than the coherent-state probe, and photon-number-resolved detection saturates this QFI. This advantage is due to the photon-loss statistics and it is still accessible for a typical overcoupled condition after averaging over fluctuations of the unresolved detuning. We identify the limits of this advantage: phase doubling does not improve resonant detuning estimation, and coincidence-only detection is inefficient close to a zero transmission. These results identify the cases in which photon pairs can be useful for absorption and pump--probe WGM sensing.

summaries.en: Using indistinguishable photon pairs in a balanced Mach-Zehnder interferometer with a lossy whispering-gallery-mode resonator yields higher quantum Fisher information than coherent states of equal mean photon number for estimating intrinsic loss and round-trip amplitude transmission at resonance away from critical coupling, an advantage arising from photon-loss statistics that persists under typical overcoupling and unresolved detuning fluctuations, though phase doubling does not improve resonant detuning estimation and coincidence-only detection is inefficient near zero transmission.
summaries.zh: 在含有有损回音壁模式谐振器的平衡马赫-曾德尔干涉仪中，使用不可区分光子对在共振且偏离临界耦合时估计本征损耗和往返振幅透射率，可获得比相同平均光子数的相干态更高的量子费舍尔信息，这一优势源于光子损耗统计，并在典型过耦合条件和未分辨失谐涨落下依然存在，但相位倍增并不能改善共振失谐估计，且仅符合计数探测在零透射附近效率低下。
summaries.ja: 損失のあるウィスパリングギャラリーモード共振器を含む平衡マッハ・ツェンダー干渉計において、臨界結合から離れた共鳴条件下で固有損失や往復振幅透過率を推定する際、同程度の平均光子数を持つコヒーレント状態よりも識別不可能な光子対を用いる方が高い量子フィッシャー情報が得られ、この利点は光子損失統計に由来して典型的な過結合条件や未分解の離調揺らぎの平均後でも維持されるが、位相倍増は共鳴離調推定を改善せず、同時計数のみの検出はゼロ透過付近で非効率である。

title: Generating entanglement in quantum matter with pathway-entangled photons via resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
abstract: Resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) is conventionally used to probe elementary excitations and correlations in quantum materials. Here, we propose an interferometric RIXS protocol that instead creates entanglement between spatially separated regions of a solid-state material. An incident X-ray photon is coherently split by a beam splitter into two arms illuminating opposite ends of a sample. Recombining the scattered photons at a second beam splitter and detecting an energy-selected photon then projects the material into a coherent superposition of excitations at the two ends. This protocol is the X-ray, solid-state analogue of the Duan-Lukin-Cirac-Zoller (DLCZ) heralding scheme. Using a Kramers-Heisenberg formalism with quantized photon modes, we show that orthogonal and degenerate end excitations yield maximally entangled states. We illustrate this mechanism in three models: (1) two decoupled sites yield a heralded Bell state. (2) An open tight-binding chain exhibits reflection-parity-dependent interference, providing a benchmark for the interferometer's coherence. (3) A spin-1 Haldane (AKLT) chain yields an entangled pair of fractionalized edge spins. We also discuss practical considerations and challenges for realizing the protocol in X-ray experiments.
subjects: Quantum Physics (quant-ph) ; Strongly Correlated Electrons (cond-mat.str-el); Optics (physics.optics)

summaries.en: An interferometric resonant inelastic X-ray scattering protocol that splits an incident X-ray photon into two arms illuminating opposite ends of a sample and recombines the scattered photons can herald entanglement between spatially separated excitations, as shown analytically for decoupled sites, an open tight-binding chain, and a spin-1 Haldane chain.
summaries.zh: 一种干涉式共振非弹性X射线散射方案通过将入射X射线光子分束为照亮样品两端的两个臂并重新组合散射光子，能够预示空间分离激发之间的纠缠，并在解耦格点、开放紧束缚链和自旋-1 Haldane链三个模型中得到演示。
summaries.ja: 入射X線光子を試料両端を照らす2本の腕に分け、散乱光子を再結合させる干渉型共鳴非弾性X線散乱プロトコルにより、空間的に離れた励起間の絡み合いを heralding でき、デカップルしたサイト、開いた強結合鎖、スピン1ハルデン鎖の3モデルで示される。

title: Pinching Antenna Systems (PASS): Principles, Positioning and Opportunities
abstract: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) have garnered significant attention owing to their ability to enhance the capacity and coverage of wireless networks by guiding electromagnetic waves through waveguides before radiation. As such, PASS are regarded as promising enabling technologies for sixth-generation (6G) communication networks. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of the state of the art in PASS, covering operating principles, positioning methodologies, performance evaluation, resource allocation, and the application of artificial intelligence (AI) to PASS-enhanced wireless networks. We first introduce the fundamental principles of PASS from both materials and physics perspectives. Building on this foundation, we present positioning methodologies for both the user side and the base station side. We then evaluate the communication performance of PASS in both uplink and downlink scenarios under different blockage models. Furthermore, we systematically review existing designs for PASS-enhanced wireless networks from a performance optimization perspective. Finally, we survey research efforts that leverage AI to address challenges in dynamic and complex scenarios.

summaries.en: This paper presents a comprehensive survey of pinching-antenna systems (PASS) for 6G networks, covering their operating principles from materials and physics perspectives, positioning methodologies for users and base stations, uplink and downlink performance evaluation under different blockage models, resource allocation and performance optimization designs, and AI-based approaches for dynamic and complex scenarios.
summaries.zh: 本文对面向6G网络的钳位天线系统（PASS）进行了全面综述，涵盖其从材料与物理角度阐述的工作原理、用户侧与基站侧的定位方法、不同阻塞模型下上下行通信性能评估、资源分配与性能优化设计，以及利用人工智能应对动态复杂场景的研究进展。
summaries.ja: 本論文は6Gネットワーク向けのピンチングアンテナシステム（PASS）に関する包括的サーベイであり、材料・物理の観点からの動作原理、ユーザ側と基地局側の測位手法、異なる遮蔽モデル下での上り・下り通信性能評価、リソース割り当てと性能最適化の設計、ならびに動的で複雑なシナリオに対応するAI活用研究を網羅している。
